hypothesis: Replacing the 4x-unrolled byte reject inside the string-skip loop of LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts L256-263 on 2fb4bdc) with an aligned Uint32Array SWAR word loop that tests each 4-byte word for a 0x22 or 0x5c lane via the haszero trick ((v - 0x01010101) & ~v & 0x80808080 on v = x ^ 0x22222222 and v = x ^ 0x5c5c5c5c), with the existing byte path kept as the unaligned head/tail and hit-word fallback, will raise the primary speedup from ~1.50 to ~1.55-1.60 (~1.05x relative), because it checks 4 string bytes per typed-array load with one combined branch instead of 4 loads and 4 compares, and it never stops on in-string bytes <= 0x5c other than quote/backslash. Chosen over rej4u32 (brief idea 3) because swarU32 has the higher median alone (~1.055 vs ~1.048 relative, its one low reading 1.014 came from a loaded process at 494 MB/s real build) and the better stack with the outer skip (1.21-1.24 vs 1.19-1.21), and its stop set is exactly the two bytes that change state, so it stays fast on real-world strings with spaces/digits/punctuation, where rej4u32 drops to the byte path. This is the only change: the escaped-carry branch, the byte tail, the outside-string switch, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion and EOF handling are untouched.

steps.change: Verification (no further edits to src; do not edit scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs, it is sealed). (a) Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm test`; all must pass with no new warnings. (b) Differential check in a temporary script OUTSIDE the repo (delete it afterwards): copy `referenceBuild` from the sealed benchmark and compare against LineIndex.build on the sealed edge fixtures plus: quote and backslash at each lane position 0-3 of a word and straddling word boundaries; backslash as the last byte of an aligned word with the escaped quote in the next word; runs of `\\` followed by `\"` of every length 1-9; trailing backslash at EOF and at every chunk end (1-byte splits); raw newline inside a string; string open at EOF with and without trailing newline; unicode/emoji strings; leading empty lines; unaligned inputs built as `Buffer.alloc(len + k).subarray(k)` for k = 0,1,2,3 with the data copied in; empty, 1-, 2- and 3-byte Buffers placed at the very end of their ArrayBuffer (`Buffer.from(new ArrayBuffer(m), m - len, len)`) to prove no RangeError; random splits of 1/2/3/5/7/64/1000 bytes; checkpointInterval 1/3/1024; array, async-iterable and string-chunk inputs. Compare checkpoints, totalBytes, totalLines, multiline flag, recordEndLines, recordEndOffsets and endsWithNewline for exact equality. (c) Run `node scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs` at least 3 times (one process each), report every run's primary and sub_scores and the median primary; correctness must be 1 in every run. Treat a run with a bimodal ratio distribution or a ref_median_mb_s far below ~550 MB/s as contention-affected and rerun it. (d) Confirm `git diff --quiet -- scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs` and that the only changed file is src/indexer/lineIndex.ts.

expected_outcome.estimated_impact: +1-8% (primary ~1.52-1.62 vs current ~1.50, central estimate ~1.58); alone it does not reach the 1.8 target; stacked later with the outer skip (skipCls) the brief measured ~1.21x relative (sealed ~1.80-1.85)
expected_outcome.rationale: After round 2, ~75% of fixture bytes are string padding handled by the 4x byte reject: 4 byte loads, 4 compares and a bounds check per 4 bytes. The aligned word loop does one Uint32Array load, two xors, and one combined haszero test per 4 bytes, with the bounds check folded into wi < wordCount. Round-3 scratch (each candidate differential-checked first, then 31 paired runs vs the sealed reference, normalized by the real build in the same process; mirror/real calibration 0.98-1.02) measured swarU32 alone at 1.077, 1.014 (loaded process), 1.047, 1.063 relative, median ~1.055, i.e. sealed ~1.58. Expected noise is ~±0.05, so the effect is near the noise floor alone; it is planned as the string-scanner half of the measured best stack (swarU32+skipCls 1.17-1.24 relative). The alignment guard, the empty-view fallback and the per-chunk view allocation (~16 chunks per build) cost nothing measurable.

sub_score_expectations.correctness: 1 (identical output on all edge fixtures, including unaligned and 1-byte-split inputs)
sub_score_expectations.cur_median_mb_s: ~870-920 MB/s (up from ~840-860 on the merged rej4 code)

history_reference.builds_on: round_2_planner_a (winner, 1.499: tight string-skip loop with 4x '> 0x5c' reject, escaped carry and byte tail, which this plan keeps except for the reject itself); research brief round_3 idea 'Aligned Uint32Array SWAR string skip (swarU32)' with its per-chunk view and alignment-guard construction, hardened here for byteOffset >= 2^31 rounding and the RangeError case of an empty view past buf.buffer.byteLength; round_1/round_2 lessons that gains must come from the in-string inner loop.
history_reference.avoids: DataView SWAR (swarDV, 0.92-0.98 relative, negative) by using a typed-array element load; 2-words-per-step SWAR (swarU32x2, 0.99) and 8x byte unroll (worse than 4x) by testing one word per step; rej4u32 (same slot, slightly weaker, not bundled); outer non-structural skip in any form (skipCls/skipLHC/skipCmp, owned by the architecture planner, separate hypothesis under H001/H003); nextCp counter and quote-before-switch (neutral); lazy/typed record storage (5-20% slower); sync scanChunk kernel and index-based chunk loop (no effect); Buffer#indexOf skipping (slower on short strings, wrong for raw newlines in strings); Uint8Array class table inside strings (slower than the plain compare).
